package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware campaign, not a package manager ecosystem)
package_info.why_malicious: The Remcos RAT delivery chain is malicious because it orchestrates a multi-stage attack exploiting Microsoft Office vulnerability CVE-2017-0199 to achieve arbitrary code execution, evade detection, establish persistence, and deploy the Remcos remote access trojan. This enables full remote control, data exfiltration, and ongoing compromise of the victim system.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Embedded OLE object triggers download of HTA file via CVE-2017-0199.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user opens the malicious Excel attachment, the embedded OLE object exploits CVE-2017-0199, initiates a remote download of an HTA file, and executes it, resulting in initial code execution on the victim system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of an OLE object to exploit a known Office vulnerability for remote code execution is a direct indicator of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Excel files do not exploit vulnerabilities or trigger downloads and execution of remote code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate use case for an Excel OLE object exploiting CVE-2017-0199.
key_indicators: Automatic download and execution of remote HTA

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: HTA file containing obfuscated JavaScript/VBScript/PowerShell to download and execute EXE.
malicious_snippets.code_language: HTA (HTML Application) with JavaScript, VBScript, PowerShell
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon execution by mshta.exe, the HTA file runs obfuscated scripts that download the malicious dllhost.exe from a remote server, writes it to disk, and executes it, escalating the attack chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: HTA files are rarely used for legitimate purposes and are a common vector for malware delivery, especially when containing obfuscated scripts that download and execute binaries.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate HTA files do not download and execute remote executables, especially using obfuscated multi-language scripts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: HTA files may be used in rare enterprise automation, but not for downloading and executing EXEs from untrusted sources.
key_indicators: Remote download and execution of EXE

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, dllhost.exe launches a PowerShell command that reads an obfuscated script from a hidden file in AppData, extracts the 'iEx' (Invoke-Expression) command, and executes the script, enabling further payload execution and maintaining obfuscation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Self-modifying and obfuscated PowerShell that reads and executes code from hidden files is a strong indicator of malicious activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate PowerShell scripts do not typically read and execute code from hidden, obfuscated files in AppData.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Advanced sysadmin automation may use PowerShell for dynamic code execution, but not with this level of obfuscation and hidden file usage.
key_indicators: Obfuscated file paths and variable names

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Copies dllhost.exe to %temp% as Vaccinerende.exe; hides PowerShell process; loads and executes code from Valvulate.Cru in memory using VirtualAlloc, MemoryCopy, CallWindowProcA.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the PowerShell payload copies dllhost.exe to %temp% as Vaccinerende.exe, hides the PowerShell process, loads additional malicious code from Valvulate.Cru into memory using native Windows API calls (VirtualAlloc, MemoryCopy, CallWindowProcA), and executes it, enabling fileless persistence and evasion.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Fileless code execution, process hiding, and in-memory loading of additional payloads are advanced evasion and persistence techniques used by malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal software does not self-replicate, hide its execution, or load and execute code from memory using these APIs.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: In-memory loaders exist for legitimate purposes, but not with this level of obfuscation and self-replication.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, Vaccinerende.exe uses ShellExecuteW to run a command that creates a registry autorun entry under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run with an obfuscated PowerShell payload, ensuring persistence by executing malicious code on user logon.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Malware frequently uses registry autorun entries with obfuscated PowerShell to maintain persistence and evade detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not create hidden autorun entries with obfuscated PowerShell commands in the registry.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise agents use autorun, but not with obfuscated or hidden PowerShell payloads.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Download and decrypt Remcos payload from hxxp://192.3.220.22/hFXELFSwRHRwqbE214.bin; inject and execute in memory using NtCreateThreadEx.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code downloads an encrypted Remcos RAT payload from a remote server, decrypts it in memory, and injects and executes it using the NtCreateThreadEx API, resulting in fileless deployment of the RAT.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Fileless deployment of a RAT via in-memory decryption and execution is a hallmark of advanced malware, designed to evade disk-based detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not download, decrypt, and execute remote code in memory using direct system calls.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate use case for this pattern.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Remcos RAT: Collects system info, keylogs, screenshots, audio, process lists; communicates with C&C server at 107.173.4.16:2404 using TLS.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the Remcos RAT operates in memory, collects sensitive data including system information, keystrokes, screenshots, audio, and process lists, and exfiltrates this data to the C&C server at 107.173.4.16:2404 over TLS, while awaiting further remote commands for full device control.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Remote access trojans are inherently malicious, enabling full remote control, data theft, and surveillance of the victim system.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate software should exfiltrate sensitive data or accept arbitrary remote commands from an external server.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate use case for this behavior.

attack_chain.action: User opens malicious Excel file, triggering CVE-2017-0199 exploit to download and execute HTA file.
HTA file executes obfuscated scripts to download and run dllhost.exe.
dllhost.exe runs obfuscated PowerShell to load further payloads from hidden files.
PowerShell code copies itself, hides execution, loads and runs further malicious code in memory.
Malicious code creates registry autorun entry for persistence.
Malicious code downloads, decrypts, and executes Remcos RAT in memory.
Remcos RAT collects data, exfiltrates to C&C, and awaits further commands.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full remote control and data exfiltration

behavioral_signatures: Office process (e.g., Excel) spawning mshta.exe or PowerShell with network activity
HTA file execution that downloads and runs EXE files from remote servers
Obfuscated PowerShell scripts reading and executing code from hidden files in AppData
Process hollowing and in-memory code injection using VirtualAlloc, MemoryCopy, CallWindowProcA, or NtCreateThreadEx
Registry autorun entries containing obfuscated PowerShell payloads
Fileless RAT deployment and outbound C&C communication to known Remcos infrastructure
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office processes (e.g., Excel) spawning mshta.exe or PowerShell, especially when accompanied by network activity. Flag HTA files that download and execute binaries from remote servers. Detect obfuscated PowerShell scripts that read and execute code from hidden files in AppData or Temp directories. Watch for process hollowing and in-memory code injection patterns using APIs such as VirtualAlloc, MemoryCopy, CallWindowProcA, or NtCreateThreadEx. Alert on suspicious autorun registry entries containing obfuscated PowerShell payloads. Monitor and block outbound connections to known Remcos C&C infrastructure and the listed IOCs.
